checks.text: Docked with 30.9 L of gel and the arm folded, womb and tail float as one egg at z -122 mm, level once the tail floods a 3.0 L trim tank in the aft end, roll GM 187 mm.

With the gel in, trim stays within 0.00 deg (arm folded 0.00, printing 0.00, baby at the lip 0.00, after the birth 0.00; positive is stern down): the tail pump moves water in the trim tank as the arm goes out (3.0 L folded, 6.2 L printing, 7.6 L at the lip, 8 L tank).
Just docked, before the gel, the egg trims -0.1 deg; during the 5 minutes the gel takes to come in the bags empty and the bore stays 17 mm above water.
The birth opening stays above the water: the lowest point of the opening is 65 mm or more above the waterline in every state.

Docking height: with 22.3 L of water in the two ballast bags the womb floats at z -142 mm and the tail at z -142 mm, so the docking faces meet within the 23 mm the cone captures (womb trim -0.6 deg). The bags empty while the gel comes in.
Before docking the womb floats with the bottom of the docking bore 14 mm above water, so no door is needed.
Docked with gel, the bottom of the bore sits 2 mm below the waterline, inside the dock seal (lip seal D 257).
The gel surface (z -135 mm) is 10 mm under the bottom of the docking bore, so no gel flows into the tail.

The kit stays where the arm sets the kit: the kit is lighter than the gel, and 2.5 Pa of yield stress is enough to stop the kit rising (the gel has 25 Pa); the three saddle feet sit in three cups on the seat.

Arm out of the tail: the boom slides the folded DexArm (passage pose, stem turned forward) through the bore; the arm stays inside R 110 mm of the R 125 mm bore, closest 14.9 mm to any part (dock collar).
Reach over the whole print: all 4302 G-code points are reached within 0.000 mm inside the official joint ranges (base -12 to 15, J1 29 to 74, J2 76 to 79 deg), boom A from -316 to -114 mm.
Collisions while printing: every link and the tool stay 15.5 mm or more from the shell, walls, chute and cradle (closest: B Fix to the bore ring; the needle in the work is left out).
Only the stem enters the gel: the lowest link is 45 mm and the tool head 31 mm above the gel surface.
After the kit is set, the stem misses every kit part except at 1 point by a pump end, 0.9 mm into the outline, where the first beads lap onto the saddle lip by design.
Kit pick and place: reached within 0.00 mm, closest 50.5 mm (womb shell), head plus fork plus kit 372 g under the 500 g payload.
Reach and clearance along the push up to the stern opening: reached within 0.00 mm, closest 15.5 mm (B Fix to the bore ring).
At the release the needle tip is 113 mm from the rim of the opening.
Push within the DexArm payload: peak 3.48 N against 4.91 N (500 g), with friction 0.3 on the chute (steepest 20 deg).

Margin on friction: with the whole body on the steepest part of the chute the push is 3.99 N at friction 0.2, 4.69 N at 0.3, 5.39 N at 0.4 and 6.80 N at 0.6; above about 0.4 the DexArm cannot climb the chute.
Stem bending at the peak push: 12G needle 106 MPa, 6 x 4 mm tube 29 MPa, against about 200 MPa yield for 304 stainless.
Telescopic boom at full reach: 443 mm beyond the rail end, tip deflection under the arm 2.3 mm (two 120 x 6 mm aluminium plates); the G-code does not correct the deflection.
Dock: the tail slows to 20 mm/s at contact; the cone centers the collar and the three FluxGrip magnets switch on after contact and hold 750 N.
The newborn drops 73 mm from the lip to the water and floats with 73 % of the 1.04 L body under water, 25 mm above the surface.
